intro: Lesson 41: Timed Paper 2 practice: the global issue, feedback and final targets. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Exam technique
points: Answer the question set, with place detail

parts.text: Specific: 'redraw spit and stack sequences from memory on Monday and Thursday'
Check: test with a 4-mark question on Friday

keywords.def: the Paper 2 Section C topic (fragile environments and climate change)
a timetable of what to revise and when

questions.q: Turn 'get better at 8-markers' into a specific target.
questions.a: e.g. 'Write one timed 8-mark answer each week with a judgement linked to criteria, and self-mark with the levels'

questions.q: Core (timed, 22 minutes), Global issue (own questions): (a) Define 'fragile environment'. (1) (b) Describe two natural causes of climate change. (4) (c) Explain how climate change may affect fragile environments. (4) (d) Assess the effectiveness of strategies to reduce deforestation in a named tropical rainforest. (8) (+ 4: explain one local response to desertification)
questions.a: (a) an environment easily damaged and slow to recover (b) Milankovitch cycles, solar output, volcanic eruptions (c) drought, higher temperatures, extreme weather, species loss (d) protected areas, monitoring, sustainable logging, enforcement limits, judgement (+) stone lines, tree planting

questions.q: Core: Self-mark, record scores, and write your final revision plan with three specific targets up to the exams.
Which is the best revision method?
questions.a: B) Testing yourself from memory. Retrieval practice strengthens memory most.

questions.q: Big question: what will you do differently in May?
questions.a: Three specific targets from today's feedback
